newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan trade houses order new Boeings for leasing.
newsitem.headline: Japan trade houses order new Boeings for leasing.

text.p: Japanese trading companies said on Tuesday they have ordered at least two dozen new Boeing Co 737-800 passenger airliners to fortify their fleets for leasing given rising demand.
Mitsui & Co Ltd said it placed orders for 10 737-800s last year with options on 10 more.
Itochu Corp said it had ordered 12 of the aircraft in June 1996, two of which would be used in a planned joint venture with Sumitomo in Dublin, Ireland.
Sumitomo Corp had ordered two 737-800s for the venture, a Sumitomo spokesman said. He declined to give the date of the order.
"There is a rise in aircraft demand. The risks are high, but we think profit is possible if operated properly," a Mitsui spokesman said.
The Sumitomo spokesman said that the venture with Itochu was expected to be established this fiscal year and that the aircraft would be leased to a Spanish airline, Air Espana SA.
A spokesman for Nissho Iwai Corp said his company plans to expand its present fleet of 15 aircraft in the future but did not give details.
All the companies declined to reveal the cost of their purchases.
